entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pope Felix IV was the bishop of Rome from 12 July 526 to his death on 22 September 530. He was the chosen candidate of Ostrogoth King Theodoric the Great, who had imprisoned Felix's predecessor, John I. 

Felix IV played a crucial role in maintaining the political and religious stability of the Western Roman Empire during a tumultuous period. He worked closely with Theodoric to secure the empire's borders and promote Christianity. 

Felix IV's legacy extends beyond his papacy, as he helped establish the Ostrogothic Kingdom and paved the way for the rise of the Byzantine Empire. His influence can still be seen in the modern-day Catholic Church.

"The Lord is near to the brokenhearted and saves the contrite of spirit." — Pope Felix IV's quote on prayer and devotion.

Felix IV's papacy was marked by significant power struggles and conflicts with the Eastern Roman Empire. Despite these challenges, he remained committed to his duties and worked tirelessly to promote the Catholic faith.
